experiment: Offline: how the cued base's hold-on rate changes with temperature (T 1.0 vs T 0.6), finished answers only.

experiment: Mechanism test against the length/error-accumulation rival: within-problem switch-marker rate per 1,000 generated tokens, finished-wrong over right samples, cued base, MATH-500, T 1.0, 4 samples. The rival (switches scale with tokens; wrong answers are only longer) predicts about 1.0; this mechanism predicts about 1.45.
recipe: File: runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-153825-208b/answers.jsonl (modal volume get iterate-runs abaybektursun-1114-153825-208b/answers.jsonl; base, cue, T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, MATH-500, 4 samples). Keep rows with attempt == 0 and sample in {0,1,2,3}; for each (problem_index, sample) keep the first row in file order. Finished = cap_hit is not true and finish_reason != 'length'; cap hits are dropped entirely. Right = finished and score_v3 == 1; finished-wrong = finished and score_v3 != 1 (0, null or missing). SW regex (Python re, case-sensitive): (?<![A-Za-z])(Alternatively|Another approach|Another way|Let me try (?:a )?(?:different|another)|Let's try (?:a )?(?:different|another)|Instead, let). S(row) = len(re.findall(SW, text)); T(row) = n_new. Eligible problems = those with at least one right and at least one finished-wrong kept row. Pool over eligible problems: S_w, T_w = sums over finished-wrong rows; S_r, T_r = sums over right rows. Statistic R = (S_w / T_w) / (S_r / T_r). If S_r == 0 the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.

experiment: Cause: base versus RL switch-marker rate per 1,000 tokens on finished MATH-500 answers at T 1.0 (RL learned to stay on one line). A reader who sees RL writing more deliberation words of every kind (result-855858, result-b4c576) expects RL at or above the base, a ratio at or below 1.0.
recipe: Files: runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-153825-208b/answers.jsonl (base, cue) and runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-183640-e828/answers.jsonl (RL, plain), both fetched with modal volume get iterate-runs <job>/answers.jsonl. In each file keep rows with attempt == 0 and sample in {0,1,2,3}, first row per (problem_index, sample) in file order, and keep only finished rows (cap_hit not true and finish_reason != 'length'), right and wrong together. SW regex, S(row) and T(row) = n_new exactly as in the first recipe. Rate(file) = sum of S / sum of T over the kept rows. Statistic = Rate(base) / Rate(RL). If the RL sum of S is 0, the statistic counts as refuted only if the base sum of S is also 0; otherwise report +infinity (not refuted).

experiment: Where the effect should not appear: the same within-problem wrong-over-right per-token switch ratio for RL-Zero-Math, whose switches (per this mechanism) come after a line is verified and so do not mark failure. The 2501.18585 reading (switching marks failure in any long-CoT model) predicts about 1.6 here as well.
recipe: File: runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-183640-e828/answers.jsonl (RL, plain, T 1.0, MATH-500, 4 samples). Apply exactly the row selection, finished/right/finished-wrong definitions, SW regex, S, T, eligible-problem rule and pooled statistic R = (S_w / T_w) / (S_r / T_r) of the first recipe to this file. experiment: Cause, the answer comes from the least-developed attempt: among the cued base's finished MATH-500 answers with exactly one switch marker, the share whose text after the switch is shorter than the text before it, finished-wrong minus right. A null in which the switch position is unrelated to correctness gives 0.
recipe: File: runs/theory-rows/abaybektursun-1114-153825-208b/answers.jsonl. Row selection, finished, right and finished-wrong as in the first recipe (attempt == 0, samples 0-3, first row per (problem_index, sample), cap hits dropped), over all problems (no eligibility filter). Keep rows with exactly one match of the SW regex of the first recipe. Let p = the start index of that match in text. Short-final = (len(text) - p) < p (characters). F_w = share of short-final among kept finished-wrong rows; F_r = share among kept right rows. Statistic = F_w - F_r. If either group has fewer than 10 rows the statistic counts as refuted.

experiment: Phenomenon on hard328 (no item reports it): among Think-SFT cue's finished, v3-wrong hard328 answers (4 single-sample full-text jobs), the share whose first non-empty text after the last 'Answer:' (or, with no marker, the last non-empty line) agrees with gold.
recipe: Files: iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1115-000503-1e5f/answers.jsonl, -000525-ea4e, -014823-ef56, -014833-1daa (fetch with modal volume get as in inventory.md); agreement function rln4_lib.agree from studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.py. In each file keep the first row per problem_index in file order. Finished = cap_hit not true and finish_reason != 'length'. Wrong = score_v3 != 1 (null or missing counts as wrong). Candidate C per row: if text contains the case-sensitive substring 'Answer:', let s = text after its last occurrence and C = the first element of s.split('\n') whose strip() is non-empty (this may be the rest of the marker line itself); if 'Answer:' is absent, C = the last element of text.split('\n') whose strip() is non-empty; if there is no such element, C = ''. Clean C: strip whitespace; remove every '$' and '*'; remove leading '\[' or '\(' and trailing '\]' or '\)'; strip a trailing '.'; if C contains '\boxed{', replace C by the brace-balanced content of its last \boxed{...}. The row counts if C is non-empty and rln4_lib.agree(C, gold) is true. Statistic = counted rows / finished wrong rows, pooled over the 4 files. Cap hits are excluded; missing rows add nothing.

experiment: Mechanism test, difficulty: the rate of layout misses per finished Think-SFT answer on problems the cued base solves at most 1 of 4 times, minus the rate on problems it solves 4 of 4. This mechanism (a fixed per-answer layout habit) predicts about 0.000. The hedged-correction rival (a second candidate added when unsure) puts these rows on hard problems and predicts about +0.015 or more. The r7-m09 easy-format account predicts a clearly negative value.
recipe: Files: the 4 Think-SFT hard328 full-text files of the first recipe, plus the 4 Think-SFT MATH-500 full-text files iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1115-000512-ee03/answers.jsonl, -014843-85d9, -000607-0e92, -000621-1d7e; studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl. In each Think-SFT file keep the first row per problem_index. Finished, wrong, candidate C, cleaning and 'layout row' (finished, wrong, C non-empty and rln4_lib.agree(C, gold) true) exactly as in the first recipe. k per problem and set: in the matching base rows.jsonl, for each sample s in {0,1,2,3} take the first row in file order with that problem_index, attempt == 0 and sample == s; k = number with score_v3 == 1 and cap_hit not true (a missing row is not right). Easy = k == 4; Hard = k <= 1; other k are dropped. Problems are matched within a set only (MATH-500 Think-SFT rows with MATH-500 base rows, hard328 with hard328). Pool all 8 files: rate_X = layout rows in stratum X / finished rows in stratum X. Statistic = rate_Hard - rate_Easy. Cap hits are excluded from both numerator and denominator; problems with no base rows are dropped.
unit: difference of fractions of finished answers

experiment: Mechanism test, what v3 read: among Think-SFT layout rows (finished, v3-wrong, gold-agreeing candidate after the last 'Answer:'), the share whose stored extracted_v3 is blank or markup only. The line-break mechanism says v3 read an empty marker line and predicts a large share. The hedged-correction rival says the 'Answer:' line held a real wrong value and predicts a small share (below 0.3).
recipe: Files: the 8 Think-SFT full-text files of the second recipe (4 hard328, 4 MATH-500). First row per problem_index per file. Layout rows exactly as in the first recipe. Blank: take extracted_v3 (null or missing counts as blank); delete all whitespace and every character in the set $ * : . , and the substrings '\[', '\]', '\(', '\)', '\boxed{}', '{}'; the row is blank if nothing remains. Statistic = blank layout rows / layout rows, pooled over the 8 files. If there are fewer than 10 layout rows, the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: Where the effect should vanish: blank v3 extractions among finished answers of the hybrid Think-SFT + 2(RL - base) minus the same share for Think-SFT itself, hard328. The mechanism says the RL delta replaces the teacher ending with a boxed line, so the hybrid's blank share falls below Think-SFT's. A reader who treats the hybrid's gain as pure finishing expects no change in the blank share of finished answers.
recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/transplant/hard328-01/rows.jsonl. Arm H = rows with arm == 'sft1_rl20' (both samples); arm T = rows with arm == 'think' (the 4 reference samples). Finished = cap_hit not true. Blank is defined on extracted_v3 exactly as in the third recipe (null or missing counts as blank). Statistic = (blank finished H rows / finished H rows) - (blank finished T rows / finished T rows). Cap hits are excluded; every row of the arm is used, with no deduplication.
unit: difference of fractions of finished answers

experiment: Mechanism test, within-problem length contrast on hard328. For each model, the mean over problems of (precision of the model's finished answers of 12,000+ tokens) minus (precision of its finished answers under 8,000 tokens), taking only problems that have both kinds. Statistic = Think-SFT's mean minus RL's. The one-axis/abstention rival (difficulty alone, no length effect within a problem) predicts about 0.00. This mechanism predicts clearly positive.
recipe: Files: T = studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01/rows.jsonl (Think-SFT cue) and R = studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_rl_plain_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl (RL plain). In each file keep rows with attempt == 0 (a missing attempt field counts as 0), then for each (problem_index, sample) the first row in file order. Finished = cap_hit not true and finish_reason != 'length'. Cap hits are excluded entirely. Right = score_v3 == 1; a finished row with null or missing score_v3 counts as wrong. Per model and problem: S = finished rows with n_new < 8000, L = finished rows with n_new >= 12000. Keep problems with at least one S row and at least one L row. d = (right rows in L / rows in L) - (right rows in S / rows in S). M_model = arithmetic mean of d over that model's kept problems (each model has its own problem set). Statistic = M_T - M_R. If either model has fewer than 5 kept problems, the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: The same lead on short problems: on MATH-500, precision of finished answers of 8,000+ tokens, Think-SFT cue minus RL plain (4 samples each, attempt 0). The board saw no lead at any coverage on MATH-500. This mechanism puts the lead wherever an answer runs long, even on MATH-500.
recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/math500_sft1_cue_s4-01/rows.jsonl (Think-SFT cue) and studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/math500_rl-01/rows.jsonl (RL plain). In each file keep rows with attempt == 0 (a missing attempt counts as 0), then the first row per (problem_index, sample) in file order. Keep finished rows (cap_hit not true and finish_reason != 'length') with n_new >= 8000. Right = score_v3 == 1 (null or missing counts as wrong). Precision per model = right kept rows / kept rows. Statistic = precision(Think-SFT) - precision(RL). If either model has fewer than 20 kept rows, the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: Where the effect should not appear: on hard328, precision of finished answers under 4,000 tokens, Think-SFT cue minus RL plain. Both models are before their drop points here, so the mechanism predicts about 0.
recipe: Files T and R as in the first recipe (thinkvote/hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01/rows.jsonl and day1_3/hard328_rl_plain_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl). attempt == 0 (missing counts as 0), first row per (problem_index, sample). Keep finished rows (cap_hit not true and finish_reason != 'length') with n_new < 4000. Right = score_v3 == 1 (null or missing = wrong). Statistic = (right / kept) for T minus (right / kept) for R.

experiment: Think-SFT holds precision up to the cap: on hard328, the precision of Think-SFT cue's finished answers of 14,000 to 16,383 tokens. An error-accumulation reading (precision keeps falling with length) puts it well under its 68 % for 12k+ answers. This mechanism keeps it near that level.
recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01/rows.jsonl. Rows with attempt == 0 (missing counts as 0), first row per (problem_index, sample) in file order. Keep finished rows (cap_hit not true and finish_reason != 'length') with 14000 <= n_new <= 16383. Statistic = (rows with score_v3 == 1) / (kept rows); null or missing score_v3 counts as wrong. If fewer than 20 rows are kept, the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: Mechanism test, flat hazard within a problem: Mantel-Haenszel rate ratio of right finishes per 1,000 alive tokens, window [12,000, 16,384) against window [4,000, 8,000), stratified by problem, for the cued base on hard328. The late-degradation rival (solve chance falls within the problem late in the answer) predicts about 0.45, near the unstratified population ratio. This mechanism predicts about 0.85 because the population fall is selection.
recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl. Keep rows with attempt == 0, then the first row in file order for each (problem_index, sample). A row is a cap hit if cap_hit is true, or cap_hit is missing and finish_reason == 'length'. A row is a right finish if score_v3 == 1 and it is not a cap hit; null or missing score_v3 is not right. Let n = n_new. Windows: early [4000, 8000), late [12000, 16384). Alive mass of a row in window [a, b) = max(0, min(n, b) - a) / 1000. Right event of a row in window [a, b) = 1 if the row is a right finish and a <= n < b, else 0. Cap hits contribute mass and never an event. For each problem p, sum over its kept rows: E_p (early events), ME_p (early mass), L_p (late events), ML_p (late mass); M_p = ME_p + ML_p. Skip problems with M_p == 0. Statistic = [sum_p L_p * ME_p / M_p] / [sum_p E_p * ML_p / M_p]. If the denominator is 0, the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: Mechanism test, spread of right-answer lengths within a problem on long problems: the median absolute log ratio of the lengths of two right attempt-0 answers to the same problem, on problems where the base hit the cap in at least one of its 4 samples. A memoryless solve time spreads right finishes across the whole window (about 0.45). A fixed-work-length rival (each problem needs about L tokens of derivation) predicts a narrow spread, about 0.2-0.25.
recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl. Keep rows with attempt == 0, then the first row in file order per (problem_index, sample). Cap hit: cap_hit true, or cap_hit missing and finish_reason == 'length'. Right finish: score_v3 == 1 and not a cap hit. Long problems: problem_index values with at least one kept cap-hit row. Among long problems keep those with at least 2 right-finish rows. For every unordered pair (i, j) of right-finish rows of the same problem, compute d = |ln(max(n_new_i, 1) / max(n_new_j, 1))|. Statistic = median of d over all pairs pooled across problems (even count: mean of the two middle values). If fewer than 5 pairs exist, the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: Cause, the per-token rate sets the cap gain: ratio of Think-SFT's pooled right-finish rate per 1,000 alive tokens in [12,000, 16,384) to the cued base's in the same window, hard328, attempt 0, 4 samples. The mechanism gives the larger 32k gain to Think-SFT because its rate is higher.
recipe: Files: A = studies/rlneurons/results/thinkvote/hard328_sft1_cue_s4-01/rows.jsonl (Think-SFT cue) and B = studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl (base cue). In each file keep rows with attempt == 0 (rows with no attempt field count as attempt 0), then the first row in file order per (problem_index, sample). Cap hit: cap_hit true, or cap_hit missing and finish_reason == 'length'. Right finish: score_v3 == 1 and not a cap hit. For each file: R = number of kept right-finish rows with 12000 <= n_new < 16384; M = sum over all kept rows of max(0, min(n_new, 16384) - 12000) / 1000. Rate = R / M. Statistic = Rate_A / Rate_B. If M or R of B is 0, the prediction counts as refuted.

experiment: Where the effect should not appear: on problems where the base is right in none of its 4 attempt-0 samples, extra tokens should buy almost nothing because the problem's own rate is near zero. Measured on fresh restarts (attempt >= 1), which under a memoryless process spend tokens at the same per-problem rate a raised cap would: the fraction of restart rows that are right.
recipe: File: studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/rows.jsonl. Attempt-0 set: rows with attempt == 0, first row in file order per (problem_index, sample). Cap hit: cap_hit true, or cap_hit missing and finish_reason == 'length'. Right: score_v3 == 1 and not a cap hit (null or missing score_v3 is not right). Z = problem_index values with at least one attempt-0 cap hit and 0 right attempt-0 rows. Restart rows = all rows with attempt >= 1 and problem_index in Z (every such row counts, file order irrelevant). Statistic = (restart rows that are right) / (restart rows). If there are no restart rows, the prediction counts as refuted.
